summary.oneLiner: Integrated power utility engaged across the electricity value chain of generation, transmission and distribution, operating across 10 Indian states and 1 Union Territory.
summary.business: Torrent Power is an integrated power utility with thermal (coal and gas-based) and renewable (solar and wind) generation, transmission, and distribution operations spanning Gujarat, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and the UT of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu. Its distribution business (licensed and franchised) serves residential, commercial and industrial customers, while its gas-based thermal units also supply RLNG to industrial consumers such as CGD, petrochemicals and fertiliser companies.

currentContext.strengths: Integrated presence across generation, transmission and distribution provides diversified, regulated earnings base|Regulated cost-plus tariff structure with assured post-tax Return on Equity (RoE)/RoCE on thermal assets (e.g., AMGEN under GERC; SUGEN/UNOSUGEN at 15.5% RoE under CERC)|High share of capacity tied under long-term PPAs (76% of SUGEN/UNOSUGEN gas capacity; renewable operational capacity fully PPA-tied)|Benchmark-low distribution losses (~2.33% in licensed areas) versus national averages, recognised with 1st rank among 65 DISCOMs (Ahmedabad, Surat circles) in Ministry of Power's 14th Integrated Ratings and Rankings|Strong credit ratings (CRISIL AA+/Stable, IND AA+/Stable long-term) supporting access to low-cost financing for expansion|Fuel security through long-term LNG procurement agreements (BP, JERA) and assured coal linkages under the Government's SHAKTI policy for new thermal capacity
currentContext.strategies: Deploy capital across thermal assets, renewables and distribution/transmission infrastructure while maintaining low leverage and delivering shareholder returns|Drive operational excellence by optimising asset utilisation, modernising networks with digital and AI-driven tools, and strengthening risk and business-continuity management|Deploy digital technologies enterprise-wide, integrating AI and analytics into grid operations and strengthening cybersecurity/data resilience|Advance responsible actions: expand renewable capacity and low-carbon solutions, enhance energy and water efficiency, and strengthen waste management/circular practices|Empower stakeholders by prioritising customer safety/satisfaction, strengthening employee engagement, and deepening community engagement and ESG standards in the supply chain|Explore emerging business opportunities such as hydrogen, energy storage and EV charging infrastructure|Scale the renewable energy (RE) portfolio, improve resource efficiency, and lower carbon footprint|Strengthen infrastructure base, reduce T&D losses, improve supply reliability, and drive innovation|The Board's core responsibilities explicitly include approving the Company's strategy and annual business priorities, major capital expenditure, acquisitions, divestments and financing arrangements, alongside oversight of enterprise risk management and financial reporting/internal controls -- i.e., capital allocation decisions are a defined Board-level governance function rather than delegated to management alone.
currentContext.expansion: Torrent Power's combined generation capacity stood at 12,044 MWp (thermal + renewable), including 1,600 MW of thermal under development, 3,950 MWp of renewable under development, 1,400 MW of thermal under acquisition, and 3,000 MW of pump storage under development. On the thermal side, the Company (via wholly owned subsidiary Newzone India Private Limited) is developing a 2x800 MW ultra-supercritical coal-based project at Anuppur, Madhya Pradesh, awarded through Case-II competitive bidding by MPPMCL at a tariff of Rs 5.829/kWh under a 25-year PPA with the State of Madhya Pradesh, with coal linkage assured under the SHAKTI Policy from SECL mines and water from the River Sone; the project involves an investment of approximately Rs 23,000 Crore, with Unit I scheduled for commissioning within 66 months and Unit II within 72 months from PPA execution. Separately, the Company has signed a definitive agreement with L&T Power Development Limited to acquire a 100% stake in Nabha Power Limited (1,400 MW supercritical coal-based capacity in Punjab, fully contracted to Punjab State Power Corporation Limited), expected to be consummated by Q1 FY27. On renewables, operational capacity reached 2,002 MWp (1,081 MWp solar, 921 MW wind) after incremental commissioning of 227 MWp solar and 29 MWp of C&I solar capacity during the year; the Company aspires to scale total renewable capacity to 10 GW by 2030 through organic and inorganic pathways, with renewable capex of ~Rs 6,010 Crore in FY26 expected to increase further in FY27. The ~3,950 MWp renewable pipeline (implemented via subsidiaries of Torrent Green Energy Private Limited, estimated investment ~Rs 27,830 Crore) includes: the MSKVY 2.0 solar project with MSEDCL (306 MW contracted / 367 MWp under installation, tariff Rs 3.10/unit, ~Rs 1,342 Crore cost; ~311 MWp commissioned as of 31 March 2026, with the PM-KUSUM commissioning deadline extended to 31 March 2027 and an extension petition pending before the Commission); the SECI Tranche XII wind project in Karnataka via Torrent Saurya Urja 2 Private Limited (300 MW, tariff Rs 2.94/unit, ~Rs 2,500 Crore cost, for which the Company has applied for a Scheduled Commercial Operation Date extension); the SECI Tranche XVI wind project in Karnataka via Torrent Solar Power Private Limited (100 MW contracted / 122 MW installation, tariff Rs 3.60/unit, ~Rs 925 Crore cost, expected commercial operation by December 2026); the SECI Tranche XVIII wind project (300 MW, tariff Rs 3.97/unit, ~Rs 2,360 Crore cost, split 175 MW in Gujarat via Torrent Saurya Urja 2 and 125 MW in Maharashtra via Torrent Solar Power, expected commissioning Q3 FY28); the TPL-D hybrid project in Gujarat via Torrent Saurya Urja 2 (450 MW contracted / 830 MWp installation, tariff Rs 3.65/unit, ~Rs 5,500 Crore cost, Phase 1 expected commercial operation September 2026 and Phase 2 March 2027); the REMCL RE-RTC project with South Eastern Railway in Maharashtra via Torrent Solar Power (100 MW contracted / 400.7 MWp installation including a 5 MW/20 MWh BESS, tariff Rs 4.25/unit, ~Rs 3,039 Crore cost, expected commercial operation by March 2027); a merchant capacity pipeline (~603 MWp under installation, ~Rs 4,664 Crore cost, to be commissioned progressively); the first FDRE project with the Company's own DISCOM (250 MW contracted / ~500 MWp installation including a 112.5 MW/450 MWh BESS, tariff Rs 4.87/unit, ~Rs 3,000 Crore cost, Scheduled Commercial Operation Date 24 months from PPA execution); and a C&I direct-supply project pipeline (~509 MW contracted / ~859 MWp under installation across multiple tariffs and offtakers, ~Rs 4,500 Crore cost, ~20.7 MWp already commissioned as of 31 March 2026). On the gas-based thermal side, the Company continues to deploy uncommitted gas capacity through merchant markets and short-term tenders calibrated to LNG economics, having successfully executed an NVVN short-term power supply contract from March to October 2025.

increasing peak demand and grid-balancing needs support merchant dispatch, but higher coal-based capacity availability and continued renewable growth (declining tariffs) may constrain contracting/dispatch opportunities for uncontracted gas capacity|Renewable capacity surge nationally (non-fossil capacity crossed 283 GW, government targeting 786 GW by FY36, annual additions expected to rise to ~50 GW/yr) underpins the Company's plan to add further capacity, considering growing demand from data centres and other loads|National AT&C losses reduced to 15.04% in FY26 from 16.12% in FY25, with regulatory focus increasing on efficiency, franchises and smart metering; the Company's own distribution losses (~2.33% in licensed areas) remain well below normative/national levels|EV adoption and charging demand growth (India EV charging demand projected to grow from ~4,000 GWh in FY25 to ~38 TWh by FY32) is being factored into distribution load forecasting and network reinforcement planning|Rising data-centre capacity in India (projected to ~6.5 GW by 2030) and associated digital/energy/cooling loads are informing the Company's capacity-addition and IT/security investment plans|Green hydrogen and energy storage policy push (National Green Hydrogen Mission target of 5 MMTPA by 2030; risks.risk: Uncontracted gas-based capacity exposed to merchant market and LNG price volatility
risks.note: 1,567 MW of the Company's 2,730 MW operational gas-based capacity is uncontracted and exposed to short-term/merchant conditions; LNG prices are inherently volatile (averaged ~USD 28/MMBtu in FY23, ~USD 11.8/MMBtu in FY26, but spiked to ~USD 20.5/MMBtu in March 2026 amid Middle East tensions), and take-or-pay/use-or-pay/ship-or-pay fuel and regasification contracts could expose the Company to charges under adverse LNG market conditions.

risks.risk: Regulatory change to gas pipeline tariffs (PNGRB 'One Nation, One Grid, One Tariff')
risks.note: The proposed unified/levelised pipeline tariff framework may be unfavourable for plants located closer to the gas source by increasing transportation charges, potentially impacting their competitiveness in merit-order dispatch.

risks.risk: AMGEN (362 MW coal plant) environmental and regulatory compliance exposure
risks.note: AMGEN is non-compliant with SOx emission norms and faces a retrospective environmental compensation charge of Rs 0.40/kWh from January 1, 2028 if it operates beyond its planned December 31, 2030 closure; it must also meet a CEA flexible-operation (minimum load) mandate by January 2030, and is in discussions with the Government of Gujarat over a proposed transfer of part of its ash pond land at Motera for a sports complex.

risks.risk: Regulatory-asset build-up and delayed cost recovery in licensed distribution
risks.note: Unrecovered regulatory claims stood at Rs 2,348 Crore (recognised) and a further Rs 1,053 Crore under dispute (not recognised) at year end; in August 2025 the Supreme Court directed DISCOMs to clear existing regulatory assets within four years and capped the regulatory asset at 3% of ARR, tightening the timeline for cash-flow recovery from tariff-related delays.

risks.risk: Execution risk in renewable energy pipeline
risks.note: Growth is constrained by difficulty acquiring suitable land for high-potential wind sites, near-saturated ISTS substation connectivity booked till 2030, and delays in obtaining Right of Use/Right of Way clearances for transmission lines, any of which can cause cost/time overruns and affect scheduled commissioning; operational renewable projects also face penalty risk from stringent scheduling and forecasting rules despite unpredictable weather.

Cybercrime, ransomware and third-party risk are flagged as key concerns; the Company has deployed AI-based EDR, UEM, WAF, Zero Trust Architecture and a Vendor Risk Management system, obtained ISO 27001:2022 certification for IT policies, and carries cyber insurance, indicating this is treated as a material ongoing exposure.

risks.risk: Rising leverage from debt-funded growth capex ahead of EBITDA accretion
risks.note: Long Term Debt to Equity increased from 0.46 to 0.67 and Net Debt to EBITDA increased from 1.41 to 2.06 year-on-year due to higher debt drawn to fund incremental capex for under-construction projects; the corresponding EBITDA accretion is only expected to start post-commissioning of these projects, creating an interim leverage/coverage lag.

guidance (verify next quarter):
- **No explicit earnings guidance given.** Capex will be "much, much higher" than FY26; declined to confirm 2x.
- 5-year aggregate capex framework confirmed: ~INR80,000 cr (RE INR28,000 cr + Coal INR23,000 cr + PSP INR14,000 cr + ~INR2,000 cr/yr distribution); roughly INR15,000–20,000 cr/yr, back-loaded to years 2–3.
- RE commissioning **1.2–1.4 GW in FY27**.
- **Nabha Power consolidation expected from Jun-2026 (Q1 FY27)** — key item to verify next quarter.
- ROE: new ROCE-based regime expected to improve effective ROE by ~1%/yr if performance milestones met.
order book & pipeline:
- Renewables 4 GW under implementation (~50% wind / 50% solar new builds); incl. SECI-12 (extension applied, COD ~before Mar-27), 367 MW MSEDCL (mostly commissioned; balance delayed by govt land relocation, ~6–9 months), 603 MW merchant (wind-tilted, no battery for now).
- Coal: 1.6 GW MP thermal — PPA with MPPMCL signed, LOA for BTG & BOP issued, EC received.
- PSP: 3 GW pumped storage — ESF agreement with MSEDCL signed, civil/hydro-mech & E&M LOAs issued, EC received.
- Transmission: Khavda commissioned this quarter; Solapur under construction.
- C&I renewables: 860 MW under construction.
segment / subsidiary:
- **Distribution** (licensed Ahmedabad/Surat + franchises): cash engine; AT&C losses ~2.5% (best-in-class); regulatory gap cut by ~INR800 cr; INR58 cr rooftop-solar incentive; carrying-cost orders recurring.
- **Gas generation**: ~50% tied to own DISCOMs on long-term PPA (fixed-cost recovery on availability); rest merchant. Historic PLF 30–35%.
- **Renewables**: GBI roll-off is the swing factor this quarter.
- **Nabha Power**: EV ~INR6,800 cr, debt ~INR3,400 cr, equity raise INR3,500–4,000 cr planned; 2-part tariff (variable pass-through).
growth verticals / optionality:
- PSP (3 GW) and battery/hybrid/RTC tilt = energy-transition / storage optionality.
- Merchant gas + merchant RE = upside when power deficit/peak pricing returns.
- Parallel licensing — no further development this quarter.
- Active interest in upcoming state thermal bids.
margins & cost dynamics:
- Generation margin compressed by scheduled-maintenance O&M (~INR40 cr) + base-effect of PY provision reversal; UNOSUGEN cap is the headline drag.
- New tariff regime: post-Apr-25 assets earn ROCE with base ROE 13% (up to 15% on milestones) vs old fixed 14%; pre-Apr-25 assets keep old framework but now also earn milestone incentives → effective ROE ~14%→15%.
- Full-year merchant + LNG gains ~INR675 cr on ~1,400 MUs.
capex / expansion:
- FY26 capex by segment: Distribution/franchise ~INR1,600 cr; Transmission ~INR550 cr; Coal ~INR700 cr; Renewables ~INR6,500 cr.
- FY27 capex to be materially higher; committed capex runs to FY31–32.
capital allocation:
- "Under-leveraged" balance sheet; leverage comfortable and "under control"; debt falls off as projects commission and EBITDA kicks in.
- Room for incremental thermal/RE bids without stressing leverage.
- Nabha funded via equity raise INR3,500–4,000 cr + existing debt.
risks & watch-items:
- UNOSUGEN PPC cap recurring (INR171 cr this Q; INR273 cr credit last Q) — appeal-dependent; timing volatility.
- LNG price (Strait of Hormuz / Iran-related) at $16–20 makes RTC merchant uneconomic; domestic gas pooled away from power sector (IOCL force majeure on Qatar gas).
- GBI exhaustion structurally lowers RE incentive income.
- Execution/transmission-line timing for 4 GW RE; MSEDCL land relocation; SECI-12 COD slippage.
- Performance-milestone risk on the new incentive-based ROE.
management quality / tone: Confident, granular, candid (e.g. openly corrected an analyst's "3 cargoes" understanding; declined to over-promise on guidance). Comfortable framing one-offs but transparent that carrying-cost income is recurring. Tone: steady, expansion-oriented.
non-obvious takeaways:
- Gas strategy is "demonstrate availability, not necessarily generate" — fixed-cost recovery hinges on availability, so spot/short-term cargoes suffice; PLF deliberately optimized to DISCOM demand. ~5 of the 10 BP/JERA cargoes (from CY27) earmarked for Torrent Power, rest for Torrent Gas.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Torrent Power is an integrated power utility with thermal (coal and gas-based) and renewable (solar and wind) generation, transmission, and distribution operations spanning Gujarat, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and the UT of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu. Its distribution business (licensed and franchised) serves residential, commercial and industrial customers, while its gas-based thermal units also supply RLNG to industrial consumers such as CGD, petrochemicals and fertiliser companies.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's electricity demand is projected to grow above 6.0% CAGR during FY26-FY36; AI, data centres and EVs are expected to push up India's peak power demand by an additional 30 GW over the next 5-6 years
- Gas-based plant utilisation will largely depend on power demand from customers, gas prices, and market opportunities; increasing peak demand and grid-balancing needs support merchant dispatch, but higher coal-based capacity availability and continued renewable growth (declining tariffs) may constrain contracting/dispatch opportunities for uncontracted gas capacity
- Renewable capacity surge nationally (non-fossil capacity crossed 283 GW, government targeting 786 GW by FY36, annual additions expected to rise to ~50 GW/yr) underpins the Company's plan to add further capacity, considering growing demand from data centres and other loads
- National AT&C losses reduced to 15.04% in FY26 from 16.12% in FY25, with regulatory focus increasing on efficiency, franchises and smart metering; the Company's own distribution losses (~2.33% in licensed areas) remain well below normative/national levels
- EV adoption and charging demand growth (India EV charging demand projected to grow from ~4,000 GWh in FY25 to ~38 TWh by FY32) is being factored into distribution load forecasting and network reinforcement planning
- Rising data-centre capacity in India (projected to ~6.5 GW by 2030) and associated digital/energy/cooling loads are informing the Company's capacity-addition and IT/security investment plans
- Green hydrogen and energy storage policy push (National Green Hydrogen Mission target of 5 MMTPA by 2030; India targeting ~80 GW BESS by FY36) is shaping the Company's pumped-storage hydro pipeline investment
- Ahmedabad's largely residential demand softened due to an extended monsoon and cooler winter; Surat and Dahej industrial demand weakened due to a slowdown in diamond and textile sectors, while DNH&DD saw momentum from heightened economic activity
- Distribution business profitability in licensed areas is governed by post-tax RoE/RoCE regulatory mechanisms rather than direct tariff-order impact, with cashflow surplus/deficit settled through quarterly FPPAS and true-up mechanisms
- Gas-based power plants continued to show high availability during FY26, aided by new digital monitoring tools for performance tracking and maintenance planning
- ~7 GWp of additional generation capacity being planned over existing operational capacity, in line with growing energy demand considering data centres and other loads
- ~8.4 GW Pumped Storage Hydro pipeline being pursued across Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh
- Solapur transmission project under construction, at an advanced stage of implementation
- ~40 kms of 400 kV D/C transmission line under pipeline, in addition to the operational network of 952 ckm (400 kV) and 388 ckm (220 kV)
- Total combined generation capacity of ~12.04 GWp including under-development and under-acquisition capacity, with ~4.0 GWp of renewables under development

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Torrent Power's combined generation capacity stood at 12,044 MWp (thermal + renewable), including 1,600 MW of thermal under development, 3,950 MWp of renewable under development, 1,400 MW of thermal under acquisition, and 3,000 MW of pump storage under development. On the thermal side, the Company (via wholly owned subsidiary Newzone India Private Limited) is developing a 2x800 MW ultra-supercritical coal-based project at Anuppur, Madhya Pradesh, awarded through Case-II competitive bidding by MPPMCL at a tariff of Rs 5.829/kWh under a 25-year PPA with the State of Madhya Pradesh, with coal linkage assured under the SHAKTI Policy from SECL mines and water from the River Sone; the project involves an investment of approximately Rs 23,000 Crore, with Unit I scheduled for commissioning within 66 months and Unit II within 72 months from PPA execution. Separately, the Company has signed a definitive agreement with L&T Power Development Limited to acquire a 100% stake in Nabha Power Limited (1,400 MW supercritical coal-based capacity in Punjab, fully contracted to Punjab State Power Corporation Limited), expected to be consummated by Q1 FY27. On renewables, operational capacity reached 2,002 MWp (1,081 MWp solar, 921 MW wind) after incremental commissioning of 227 MWp solar and 29 MWp of C&I solar capacity during the year; the Company aspires to scale total renewable capacity to 10 GW by 2030 through organic and inorganic pathways, with renewable capex of ~Rs 6,010 Crore in FY26 expected to increase further in FY27. The ~3,950 MWp renewable pipeline (implemented via subsidiaries of Torrent Green Energy Private Limited, estimated investment ~Rs 27,830 Crore) includes: the MSKVY 2.0 solar project with MSEDCL (306 MW contracted / 367 MWp under installation, tariff Rs 3.10/unit, ~Rs 1,342 Crore cost; ~311 MWp commissioned as of 31 March 2026, with the PM-KUSUM commissioning deadline extended to 31 March 2027 and an extension petition pending before the Commission); the SECI Tranche XII wind project in Karnataka via Torrent Saurya Urja 2 Private Limited (300 MW, tariff Rs 2.94/unit, ~Rs 2,500 Crore cost, for which the Company has applied for a Scheduled Commercial Operation Date extension); the SECI Tranche XVI wind project in Karnataka via Torrent Solar Power Private Limited (100 MW contracted / 122 MW installation, tariff Rs 3.60/unit, ~Rs 925 Crore cost, expected commercial operation by December 2026); the SECI Tranche XVIII wind project (300 MW, tariff Rs 3.97/unit, ~Rs 2,360 Crore cost, split 175 MW in Gujarat via Torrent Saurya Urja 2 and 125 MW in Maharashtra via Torrent Solar Power, expected commissioning Q3 FY28); the TPL-D hybrid project in Gujarat via Torrent Saurya Urja 2 (450 MW contracted / 830 MWp installation, tariff Rs 3.65/unit, ~Rs 5,500 Crore cost, Phase 1 expected commercial operation September 2026 and Phase 2 March 2027); the REMCL RE-RTC project with South Eastern Railway in Maharashtra via Torrent Solar Power (100 MW contracted / 400.7 MWp installation including a 5 MW/20 MWh BESS, tariff Rs 4.25/unit, ~Rs 3,039 Crore cost, expected commercial operation by March 2027); a merchant capacity pipeline (~603 MWp under installation, ~Rs 4,664 Crore cost, to be commissioned progressively); the first FDRE project with the Company's own DISCOM (250 MW contracted / ~500 MWp installation including a 112.5 MW/450 MWh BESS, tariff Rs 4.87/unit, ~Rs 3,000 Crore cost, Scheduled Commercial Operation Date 24 months from PPA execution); and a C&I direct-supply project pipeline (~509 MW contracted / ~859 MWp under installation across multiple tariffs and offtakers, ~Rs 4,500 Crore cost, ~20.7 MWp already commissioned as of 31 March 2026). On the gas-based thermal side, the Company continues to deploy uncommitted gas capacity through merchant markets and short-term tenders calibrated to LNG economics, having successfully executed an NVVN short-term power supply contract from March to October 2025.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident, granular, candid (e.g. openly corrected an analyst's "3 cargoes" understanding; declined to over-promise on guidance). Comfortable framing one-offs but transparent that carrying-cost income is recurring. Tone: steady, expansion-oriented.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Integrated presence across generation, transmission and distribution provides diversified, regulated earnings base
- Regulated cost-plus tariff structure with assured post-tax Return on Equity (RoE)/RoCE on thermal assets (e.g., AMGEN under GERC; SUGEN/UNOSUGEN at 15.5% RoE under CERC)
- High share of capacity tied under long-term PPAs (76% of SUGEN/UNOSUGEN gas capacity; renewable operational capacity fully PPA-tied)
- Benchmark-low distribution losses (~2.33% in licensed areas) versus national averages, recognised with 1st rank among 65 DISCOMs (Ahmedabad, Surat circles) in Ministry of Power's 14th Integrated Ratings and Rankings
- Strong credit ratings (CRISIL AA+/Stable, IND AA+/Stable long-term) supporting access to low-cost financing for expansion
- Fuel security through long-term LNG procurement agreements (BP, JERA) and assured coal linkages under the Government's SHAKTI policy for new thermal capacity

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
- UNOSUGEN PPC cap recurring (INR171 cr this Q; INR273 cr credit last Q) — appeal-dependent; timing volatility.
- LNG price (Strait of Hormuz / Iran-related) at $16–20 makes RTC merchant uneconomic; domestic gas pooled away from power sector (IOCL force majeure on Qatar gas).
- GBI exhaustion structurally lowers RE incentive income.
- Execution/transmission-line timing for 4 GW RE; MSEDCL land relocation; SECI-12 COD slippage.
- Performance-milestone risk on the new incentive-based ROE.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- Gas strategy is "demonstrate availability, not necessarily generate" — fixed-cost recovery hinges on availability, so spot/short-term cargoes suffice; PLF deliberately optimized to DISCOM demand. ~5 of the 10 BP/JERA cargoes (from CY27) earmarked for Torrent Power, rest for Torrent Gas.
- The INR186 cr carrying cost is NOT treated as a one-off by mgmt — bulls modelling "clean" EBITDA should not strip it.
- Merchant 603 MW RE may convert to contracted as bids are won — not permanently merchant.
- Batteries on existing hybrid/RTC projects are small; no major config/IRR shift expected near-term.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Deploy capital across thermal assets, renewables and distribution/transmission infrastructure while maintaining low leverage and delivering shareholder returns
- Drive operational excellence by optimising asset utilisation, modernising networks with digital and AI-driven tools, and strengthening risk and business-continuity management
- Deploy digital technologies enterprise-wide, integrating AI and analytics into grid operations and strengthening cybersecurity/data resilience
- Advance responsible actions: expand renewable capacity and low-carbon solutions, enhance energy and water efficiency, and …

qoq_log.title: QoQ change log
qoq_log.body:
- UNOSUGEN: Q2/prior quarter booked a +INR273 cr credit (cap removed in TP's favour); this quarter takes a −INR171 cr provision (cap re-imposed for FY24-25 true-up) — same recurring contest, opposite sign.
- Generation swung to reported EBITDA loss (−INR39 cr) vs prior positive, on the provision + scheduled maintenance + base effect.
- Khavda transmission commissioned this quarter (new vs pipeline prior).
- Coal MP project advanced: PPA signed, BTG/BOP LOA, EC received (milestones newly hit).
- PSP advanced: ESF agreement, civil/E&M LOAs, EC received.
- Nabha acquisition moved from announced to CP-compliance, consolidation now guided for Jun-2026.
- Summer gas: 2 of 3 contracted cargoes received (non-Persian-Gulf source), 3rd due June.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Acquisition] Nabha Power - a 1,400 MW (2 x 700) supercritical coal plant at Patiala, Punjab with a 25-year PSPCL PPA set up under Case II Competitive Bidding Guidelines - was acquired with effect from 25.06.2026 and is included in the 30.06.2026 capacity figures.
- [Group asset, not TPL] Torrent Gas Limited, incorporated in FY19, has 17 operating Geographical Areas across 34 districts, 7 states and 1 Union Territory, >17,270 inch-km steel pipeline, >8,100 km MDPE pipeline, >500 CNG stations and more than 2.10 lac PNG domestic connections - these are group, not listed-entity, assets.
- [Fuel security] Amgen has a Fuel Supply Agreement with SECL and Nabha long-term FSAs with SECL and NCL; Anuppur's coal supply is "Arranged by MPPMCL under the SHAKTI Policy of Ministry of Coal".
